subtopic: The 2008 Auction Rate Securities Market Collapse
source_evidence: ARS did not have the same level of liquidity as those other instruments.
question: Misconception: Because auction rate securities were marketed as “cash-equivalent,” investors could always sell them as easily as money market mutual funds or certificates of deposit. What is the correction?
answer: “Cash-equivalent” was how ARS were marketed, but they did not have the same level of liquidity as money market mutual funds or certificates of deposit. During the 2008 market collapse, some investors could not sell their ARS until an auction succeeded.
